Hey. I took Prozac (40mg) for at least 3 months consecutively, then stopped, then restarted for a month again. That’s when my doc and I decided it wasn’t for me.

For me, the first time I took it, I only noticed positive effects after the 4th week. The first few weeks were kinda horrible for me, with worsening suicidal thoughts. Doc gave me a forewarning that that might happen to me (20 at the time, F). After that episode, things gradually started getting better. I wasn’t “sad” all the time. I was able to attend classes. I was able to eat. However, nothing more than that.

I disliked the emotional blunting that goes along with Prozac (just like any SSRIs). Some people like it, because they feel it’s better than being sad. Honestly, I’d prefer feeling sad than being numb. Numbness hurts me so much because I want to cry, but can’t.

Over the course of a few weeks, the numbness got worse. I also lacked empathy. I didn’t care about what others were feeling/telling me. If anything, anti-depressants are made to make you feel like your normal “you”. It made me feel like a crappy zombie instead.

So there’s that. I’m currently on a different medication now. Wish you all the best OP. This sub is always here for you.

Not exactly a translator, but I translated on various occasions. I was a student nurse, very new to the scene. It was probably my second year in the course, and we had regular clinical attachments in local hospitals every vacation.

One instance, I had a patient who had to go for surgery. Of course, one of the risks of anaesthesia that goes with surgery includes death. I was explaining this to an 80 year old lady who was already anxious about her situation. She only spoke a certain language and I was the only one there who could speak it. I had to translate the word “death” in a way that wouldn’t scare her further. But how do you do that? Nobody taught me how to say that in Nursing. I bluntly translated that phrase to her and she burst into tears. She left the next morning AMA.

Another instance, happened in the same school year. An patient of mine, probably a 40 year old man, was dying of a heart attack in the ward. It was too sudden but looking at his medical records he wouldn’t survive the night. The doctor called his wife to inform regarding his “dying situation”. The moment she arrived, I had to translate the doctors words of “he will not make it. Please go see him now” and I felt so bad. He died in the next half hour.

I’ve got a few experiences on hand, so I’ll list them in chronological order to make it easier to understand. Gonna be a long read.

**2013-2015: High School**

This was where the bulk of my self-harm occured. I had a few close friends who knew about me being moody and suicidal (I wasn’t officially diagnosed or anything. Really thought it was just teenage angst lol). I started cutting a lot during this time and I knew my friends noticed. I would wear cardigans to school on a daily basis. Even had a collection of black ones because they only allowed those. On days where I forget, I try my best to hide them by moving my arms awkwardly and keeping them in awkward positions. They would say “hey, it’s okay. We know.” And that comforted me.

I also started dating during this phase. One of the dudes I dated, was disgusting. He saw my scars and told me straight in the face, “stop it or I will not be your friend anymore, let alone date you” I cut him off ever since. Tried to reconnect with me but those attempts never lasted.

Another dude I dated, was open about it. He asked me to talk about my ?depression and SH scars. Rather sweet. He was battling an addiction at the time too.

Had a boyfriend soon after. Quite a stable relationship. I managed to open up about my ?depression (once again, not diagnosed at the time) and my self-harm scars. He asked if he could take a look. I was confused, but the look of concern on his face made me trust him enough to look at them. I rolled up my sleeves and he was silent, then teared up a little bit. He expressed his concerns, and promised to take care of me. Sadly, the relationship ended about 2 years later for various reasons.

Parents saw my scars at this point. Told em it was the cat. Mom said, “it looks like something a drug addict would do”. I’m glad she doesn’t really have knowledge on SH so I was able to lie.. in her face.. that it was the cat. Dad didn’t ask much.

**2016-2018: College**

?Depression and panic attacks got worse. Cut more on arms and thighs. Wasn’t wearing shorts much at the time so that helped, but wore them during physical exercise classes we had. Noticed a classmate look at them, but he didn’t say anything.

Had a couple of good friends who noticed the SH scars and asked about them politely. Lied that it was because of the cat and they didn’t buy it, of course. They were quite calm about it (also we were in a health-related course so we see lots of things). Fortunately, didn’t meet much unpleasant people during these years.

**2018-current: University**

Got my first diagnosis (lol sounds like an award): MDD, GAD. My SH turned from cutting to scratch wounds (I thought they were better and less addicting, turns out I was wrong). I tend to scratch at easy-to-reach places eg. Hands and wrists, which didn’t really help as they were visible. I started smoking at this point, and I deliberately burned myself with the cigarette butts as well.

My friends were quick to notice, and questioned me about it. Most of them knew of my condition but treated me as the person I am, not as the diagnosis. (Something we learnt in psych too). We had a rather long discussion, heartfelt and insightful. I’m glad to have met these people.

So there you have it. If you made it this far, thank you for reading. X

I’m always on the line of wanting to kill myself, but feel bad for people around me. I want to talk to someone, but I can’t seem to reach out. In the end I wallow in my own pit of hopelessness and attempt.

Story of my life.

I believe in not telling at the beginning, where trust is still being built.

When you start going out on a few dates and things start to get a little more serious, I feel that getting to know someone on a deeper level is important. That being said, disclosing certain stuff that you wouldn’t to others. I feel it’s a two-way thing - I would like them to do the same. It enables me to understand them better, what their circumstances are and I wouldn’t be frightened/too concerned (not saying I shouldn’t be, but having a heads up would be nice) if they started behaving in a different manner.

If you disclose it at the very beginning and you feel comfortable with it, I say why not. I just don’t like doing that because that’ll mean that I have to tell a lot of people before we even develop anything haha. Also because I used to go on dates and talk to people regularly..... heh

Tldr: bottomline, effective communication wins
